items.q: Retail media is advertising shown on a retailer’s own sites, apps or stores.
items.why: The retailer sells ad space on the places where its shoppers already are.

items.q: Retail media advertisers can often see sales results linked to their ads.
items.why: Because the retailer sees the purchase, it can link an ad to a sale.

items.q: Sponsored product ads appear among search results or on product pages.
items.why: They look like products and are usually labelled as ads.

items.q: Retail media only ever runs on websites, never in physical stores.
items.why: Many retailers also sell in-store screens and other formats.

items.q: Closed-loop measurement links ad exposure to actual purchases.
items.why: It closes the loop between seeing an ad and buying.

items.q: Retailers use first-party data from their own customers to target retail media.
items.why: Purchase history and browsing on the retailer’s own channels are key inputs.

items.q: Offsite retail media shows ads away from the retailer’s own channels, using the retailer’s audiences.
items.why: A brand can reach the same shoppers on other sites and apps.

items.q: Retail media ROAS can be compared across retailers without checking how each one defines it.
items.why: Definitions of sales and attribution windows differ, so numbers are not always comparable.

items.q: Brands often bid for keywords on a retailer’s search results.
items.why: The higher the bid and relevance, the better the position.

items.q: Retail media only helps brands that sell in the same store as the ad.
items.why: Offsite formats and measurement can support wider goals, though the retailer’s own sales are what it sees best.
